market_outlook: This is a company-specific earnings note focused on Tuesday BMO reporters. No broad directional market view is provided in this edition.

company_items.summary: FQ4 EPS of $56.05 beat the Street's $54.03, but the quality was low — the beat was driven by a 145bp tariff refund tailwind and 105bp non-cash LIFO benefit to gross margins. Domestic comps came in at +1.6% vs. the Street's +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio rose 100bp Y/Y to 33.4% of sales. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks and expressed confidence heading into F27.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500MM upfront plus an additional ~$106.5MM. RealSense is expected to generate $80-90MM in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex in the fast-growing Physical AI and robotics perception market.

FQ1 EPS of 53c significantly beat the Street's 36c estimate, and importantly the beat holds up even excluding an 11-cent tariff refund tailwind — core EPS was 42c vs. 36c expected. Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4MM vs. the Street's $943.2MM, though orders rose 3.5% Y/Y. F27 revenue guidance was trimmed to $3.88-4.03B from $3.93-4.13B, while EPS guidance of $1.85-2.15 was held unchanged and FQ2 EPS guidance midpoint of 46c is in line with consensus.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO, effective November 1st, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. The announcement is a leadership change with no financial results involved.

FQ4 EPS of 78c missed the Street's 87c estimate as gross margins fell 230bp Y/Y to 12.4% versus the 13.85% expected, with management citing stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressure squeezing consumers. Revenue of $2.311B came in above the Street's $2.17B estimate but still declined 8.4% year-over-year. Some bright spots include healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost reduction actions underway, and a surge of roughly 75% Y/Y in North American towable RV order backlog, though the company declined to issue formal F27 guidance.

Viking shares spiked in pre-market trading after reporting positive Phase trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. The strong efficacy data reinforces Viking's competitive positioning in the increasingly crowded but high-value obesity drug market. This is a significant clinical catalyst for the stock.

sectors: RV/recreational vehicle sector facing headwinds from stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation per THOR Industries commentary. GLP-1/obesity drug space sees renewed momentum on Viking's positive VK2735 trial data showing 22% weight loss.
tts_summary:
Good morning. This edition is a focused company-specific note covering Tuesday before-the-open reporters — no broad macro or index commentary is included today, so let's go straight to the names.

Starting with AutoZone. The company posted fiscal fourth quarter earnings of fifty-six dollars and five cents per share, beating the Street's fifty-four dollar and three cent estimate. But here's the catch — the quality of that beat is low. The outperformance was driven by a one hundred forty-five basis point tailwind to gross margins from tariff refunds and a one hundred five basis point non-cash LIFO benefit. Strip those out, and the picture softens considerably. Domestic comps came in at plus one point six percent versus the Street's plus three point one percent, and the operating expense ratio rose one hundred basis points year-over-year. Management did flag improving sales trends in the back half of the quarter and expressed confidence heading into fiscal twenty-seven — but the core miss on comps keeps this a mixed read.

Cognex is buying RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision tech for robotic perception and Physical AI, for roughly five hundred million dollars upfront plus about one hundred and six and a half million more. RealSense is tracking eighty to ninety million dollars in revenue at over fifty percent year-over-year growth. This is a meaningful strategic bet on the robotics and Physical AI buildout — directionally bullish for Cognex.

MillerKnoll delivered a strong earnings beat — fifty-three cents versus the Street's thirty-six cents — and importantly, even backing out the eleven-cent tariff refund tailwind, core EPS was forty-two cents, still well ahead of estimates. Sales missed at nine hundred twenty-three million versus nine forty-three expected, but orders rose three and a half percent year-over-year. Full-year revenue guidance was trimmed modestly, but EPS guidance was held. Call it mixed but leaning positive on the earnings quality story.

THOR Industries missed on the bottom line — seventy-eight cents versus eighty-seven cents expected — as gross margins fell two hundred thirty basis points year-over-year. Management was candid about the tough consumer backdrop: stubborn rates, high fuel costs, inflation. They're not providing formal fiscal twenty-seven guidance yet. The silver lining is North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly seventy-five percent year-over-year, and structural cost actions are underway. Still, the overall tone is cautious.

Finally, Viking Therapeutics is the pre-market standout. Shares are spiking after the company reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735 — twenty-two percent weight loss. That is a strong efficacy number and a clear positive catalyst in the obesity drug race.

Bottom line for today: no broad market signal in this note, but Viking's GLP-1 data is the headline mover, AutoZone's beat needs scrutiny on quality, and the RV space remains under macro pressure.
